title: dedicated-autoscaler: smoother burst controls and per-fleet utilization reporting
author: Lucas Hart
description:
Context: Dedicated fleets were experiencing transient latency spikes during short burst periods and the fleet autoscaler lacked visibility into short-window utilization. This PR introduces a smoother burst-control policy (token-bucket smoothing + leaky bucket fallback), per-fleet short-window utilization metrics, and wiring to the Console and alerts.

Motivation: Reduce latency/regression risk during bursts while keeping throughput guarantees predictable and expose better utilization data for capacity planning. This work is part of ENG-3621 and builds on prior tokenbucket smoothing experiments.

What changed (high level):
- Implement token-bucket smoothing with configurable smoothing_window_ms and alpha smoothing parameter
- Add leaky-bucket fallback for extreme overload cases to prevent queue blowup
- Emit new metrics: dedicated_fleet.utilization.short_window_p50/95/99, dedicated_fleet.tokenbucket_fill, dedicated_fleet.smoother_drops
- Expose short-window utilization and tokenbucket metrics in Console per-fleet view and add a small chart
- Add integration tests for smoothing behavior and unit tests for metric calculations
- Add migration that safely adds smoothing config defaults for existing fleets

Notes: Feature is behind a runtime config flag (autoscaler.smoothing.enabled=false by default) and rollout plan is to enable for a subset of fleets, monitor, then gradual roll out.
